Ravi: Quick brain-dump: propose an "attestable parcel" for air-gapped/on-prem upgrades. Parcel = micro-manifest + content-addressed chunks + compact proofs + signed header. Goal: operator-friendly inspection on removable media and partial apply for constrained nodes.
Sasha: sounds useful. how is this different from past bundles?
Ravi: focus on minimal inspectable metadata (no full extract), chunk-possession attestations for staged syncs, and explicit activation phases so rollback is cheap.
Lina: signer rotation is tricky for offline sites. we need an offline rotation snapshot or a trust-bundle that ops refreshes manually.
Tom: agree. parcel header should include signer id, epoch, and optional rotation appendix. offline sites can maintain a trust.json.
Sasha: operator UX: `rbox parcel inspect-lite /mnt/usb/update.apf` -> prints header, components, chunk counts, required disk. no extraction.
Ravi: proofs must scale with changed-chunk-count not model size. use chunk-level Merkle and only include changed-leaf paths. sample proofs allowed for quick triage but require full proofs before activation.
Lina: apply model: A/B slots. stream changed chunks to candidate slot, verify, then atomic pointer flip. rollback = flip back. GC keeps previous chunks until policy expires.
Tom: DOS mitigations: enforce max-chunk-count, min-chunk-size, and worst-case-cost estimate during inspect. Console should surface rejects.
Sasha: Dedicated can run a verifier service that issues short attestation tokens. Private sites run sidecar verifier.
Ravi: CLI examples to include in RFC appendix and operator playbook. Lina + Ravi to own docs.
